{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_ef1640e7fe904ffdad5f13b7","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t![NEEDLE](docs/hero.png)\n2\t\n3\t# 🧵 NEEDLE\n4\t\n5\t[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\n6\t[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)\n7\t[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.4.0-green.svg)](Cargo.toml)\n8\t\n9\t**N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\n10\t\n11\t> Deterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\n12\t\n13\tNEEDLE is a universal wrapper for headless coding CLI agents. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## 🚀 Quickstart\n18\t\n19\t```bash\n20\t# Install the latest release (prebuilt binary, Linux x86_64/aarch64)\n21\tcurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\n22\t\n23\t# Or build from source (needs Rust 1.75+, see rust-toolchain.toml)\n24\tcargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\n25\t\n26\t# Configure your bead workspace backend (required)\n27\tcd /path/to/your/workspace\n28\tcat > .needle.yaml << 'EOF'\n29\tbead_cli:\n30\t  backend: bead-rs  # or 'bead-forge' for legacy bf/br workspaces\n31\tEOF\n32\t\n33\t# Run a worker\n34\tneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\n35\t```\n36\t\n37\tThe installer drops `needle` in `~/.local/bin` (override with `NEEDLE_INSTALL_PATH`);\n38\tmake sure that directory is on your `PATH`.\n39\t\n40\tA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\n41\t\n42\tSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\n43\t\n44\t---\n45\t\n46\t## 🧶 What is a bead?\n47\t\n48\tA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\n49\t\n50\tBeads live in a **bead store** — a pluggable backend managed by a bead CLI. The current primary backend is **bead-rs**, which uses a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a checkpoint directory (`.beads/checkpoint/` with `current.json`, `forensic.jsonl`, and `objects/`). The legacy **bead-forge** backend uses `issues.jsonl`.\n51\t\n52\t```bash\n53\t# Create a bead (bead-rs backend)\n54\tbead create --title \"Add pagination to search results\" --priority 2 --issue-type task\n55\t\n56\t# List open beads\n57\tbead list --status open\n58\t\n59\t# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\n60\t```\n61\t\n62\tNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\n63\t\n64\t---\n65\t\n66\t## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\n67\t\n68\tExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\n69\t\n70\t- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\n71\t- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\n72\t\n73\tNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\n74\t\n75\t---\n76\t\n77\t## 🧠 Core Principle\n78\t\n79\tNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\n80\t\n81\t```\n82\tIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\n83\tIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\n84\t```\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\n89\t\n90\tA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\n91\t\n92\t```\n93\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n94\t│                                                     │\n95\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n96\t│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\n97\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\n98\t│         │                                        │  │\n99\t│         ▼                                        │  │\n100\t│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\n101\t│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\n102\t│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\n103\t│         │ claimed                                   │\n104\t│         ▼                                           │\n105\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n106\t│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\n107\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n108\t│         │                                           │\n109\t│         ▼                                           │\n110\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n111\t│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\n112\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n113\t│         │                                           │\n114\t│         ▼                                           │\n115\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n116\t│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\n117\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n118\t│         │                                           │\n119\t│         ▼                                           │\n120\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n121\t│   │ 📊 OUTCOME │                                     │\n122\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n123\t│         │                                           │\n124\t│         ├── ✅ success ──► close bead ──────────────┘\n125\t│         ├── ❌ failure ──► log + release ────────────┘\n126\t│         ├── ⏰ timeout ──► release + defer ──────────┘\n127\t│         └── 💀 crash ────► release + alert ──────────┘\n128\t│                                                     │\n129\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n130\t```\n131\t\n132\t---\n133\t\n134\t## 📐 Algorithm Steps\n135\t\n136\t### 🔍 Step 1: Select\n137\t\n138\tQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\n139\t\n140\t### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\n141\t\n142\tAttempt an **atomic claim** via the bead CLI (`bead claim` for bead-rs, `bf claim` for bead-forge). SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\n143\t\n144\t### 📋 Step 3: Build\n145\t\n146\tConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\n147\t\n148\t### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\n149\t\n150\tLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\n151\t\n152\t### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\n153\t\n154\tThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\n155\t\n156\t### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\n157\t\n158\tEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\n159\t\n160\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\n161\t|---------|-----------|---------|\n162\t| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\n163\t| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\n164\t| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\n165\t| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\n166\t| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\n167\t| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\n168\t\n169\tEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\n170\t\n171\t---\n172\t\n173\t## 🧶 Strand Escalation\n174\t\n175\tWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. A silent worker is a broken worker.\n313\t\n314\t### Exported Signals\n315\t\n316\t| Signal | Description |\n317\t|--------|-------------|\n318\t| **Traces** | Spans for `worker.session`, `bead.lifecycle`, `bead.claim`, `agent.dispatch`, `strand.evaluated`, `outcome.handled` |\n319\t| **Metrics** | `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.cost.usd`, and more |\n320\t| **Logs** | All events not represented as spans, with severity mapping (`ERROR` for failures, `WARN` for stale peers) |\n321\t\n322\t### OpenTelemetry (OTLP) Export\n323\t\n324\tNEEDLE can export telemetry to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.) via OTLP.\n325\t\n326\t**Minimal configuration (`.needle.yaml`):**\n327\t\n328\t```yaml\n329\ttelemetry:\n330\t  otlp_sink:\n331\t    enabled: true\n332\t    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC, or :4318 for HTTP\n333\t    protocol: \"grpc\"\n334\t```\n335\t\n336\t**Semantic conventions:** NEEDLE follows OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions for LLM telemetry, enabling out-of-the-box integration with GenAI dashboards (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n337\t\n338\tSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) for the complete semantic mapping table.\n339\t\n340\t---\n341\t\n342\t## 📊 Production Status\n343\t\n344\tNEEDLE currently powers my own headless multi-agent workflow — workers run continuously against shared bead queues, dispatching to Claude Code and other CLIs, with full OTLP telemetry wired through. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\n\n---\n\n## 🚀 Quickstart\n\n```bash\n# Install the latest release (prebuilt binary, Linux x86_64/aarch64)\ncurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\n\n# Or build from source (needs Rust 1.75+, see rust-toolchain.toml)\ncargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\n\n# Configure your bead workspace backend (required)\ncd /path/to/your/workspace\ncat > .needle.yaml << 'EOF'\nbead_cli:\n  backend: bead-rs  # or 'bead-forge' for legacy bf/br workspaces\nEOF\n\n# Run a worker\nneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\n```\n\nThe installer drops `needle` in `~/.local/bin` (override with `NEEDLE_INSTALL_PATH`);\nmake sure that directory is on your `PATH`.\n\nA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\n\nSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\n\n---\n\n## 🧶 What is a bead?\n\nA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\n\nBeads live in a **bead store** — a pluggable backend managed by a bead CLI. The current primary backend is **bead-rs**, which uses a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a checkpoint directory (`.beads/checkpoint/` with `current.json`, `forensic.jsonl`, and `objects/`). The legacy **bead-forge** backend uses `issues.jsonl`.\n\n```bash\n# Create a bead (bead-rs backend)\nbead create --title \"Add pagination to search results\" --priority 2 --issue-type task\n\n# List open beads\nbead list --status open\n\n# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\n```\n\nNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\n\n---\n\n## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\n\nExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\n\n- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\n- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\n\nNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\n\n---\n\n## 🧠 Core Principle\n\nNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\n\n```\nIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\nIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\n```\n\n---\n\n## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\n\nA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                     │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\n│         │                                        │  │\n│         ▼                                        │  │\n│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\n│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\n│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\n│         │ claimed                                   │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ▼                                           │\n│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n│   │ 📊 OUTCOME │                                     │\n│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n│         │                                           │\n│         ├── ✅ success ──► close bead ──────────────┘\n│         ├── ❌ failure ──► log + release ────────────┘\n│         ├── ⏰ timeout ──► release + defer ──────────┘\n│         └── 💀 crash ────► release + alert ──────────┘\n│                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 📐 Algorithm Steps\n\n### 🔍 Step 1: Select\n\nQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\n\n### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\n\nAttempt an **atomic claim** via the bead CLI (`bead claim` for bead-rs, `bf claim` for bead-forge). SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\n\n### 📋 Step 3: Build\n\nConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\n\n### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\n\nLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\n\n### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\n\nThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\n\n### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\n\nEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\n\n| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\n|---------|-----------|---------|\n| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\n| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\n| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\n| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\n| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\n| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\n\nEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\n\n---\n\n## 🧶 Strand Escalation\n\nWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. Each strand is evaluated in order — the first strand that yields a bead wins.\n\n| # | Strand | Agent? | Purpose |\n|---|--------|--------|---------|\n| 1 | 🪡 **Pluck** | Yes | Process beads from the assigned workspace |\n| 2 | 🔧 **Mend** | No | Cleanup: orphaned claims, stale locks, health checks |\n| 3 | 🔭 **Explore** | No | Search other workspaces for claimable beads |\n| 4 | 🕸️ **Weave** | Yes | Create beads from documentation gaps *(opt-in)* |\n| 5 | 🪢 **Unravel** | Yes | Propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads *(opt-in)* |\n| 6 | 💓 **Pulse** | Yes | Codebase health scans, auto-generate beads *(opt-in)* |\n| 7 | 🪞 **Reflect** | Yes | Consolidate learnings from recent beads *(opt-in)* |\n| 8 | 🪡 **Splice** | No | Document worker failures, create alert beads |\n| 9 | 🪢 **Knot** | No | All strands exhausted — alert human, wait |\n\n---\n\n## ⚡ Parallel Workers\n\nMultiple NEEDLE workers run independently with **no central orchestrator**. Coordination happens through the shared bead queue:\n\n- **Atomicity** — the bead CLI's claim command uses SQLite transactions; exactly one worker wins each claim\n- **Determinism** — all workers compute the same priority order; races are resolved by the database, not by timing\n- **Independence** — each worker is a self-contained loop in its own tmux session\n- **Naming** — workers use NATO alphabet identifiers: `alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, ...\n\n```\n  needle-claude-sonnet-alpha ──┐\n  needle-claude-sonnet-bravo ──┤\n  needle-codex-gpt4-charlie ───┼──► Shared .beads/ (SQLite + checkpoint)\n  needle-opencode-qwen-delta ──┤\n  needle-aider-sonnet-echo ────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 🏗️ Supported Agents\n\nNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. Any CLI that accepts a prompt and exits works.\n\n| Agent | CLI | Input Method | Notes |\n|-------|-----|-------------|-------|\n| Claude Code (interactive) | `claude-interactive` | stdin | **Recommended** — uses subscription billing; see [plugin](#-claude-interactive-plugin) |\n| Claude Code (API) | `claude --print` | stdin | Uses programmatic/API billing |\n| OpenCode | `opencode` | file | |\n| Codex CLI | `codex` | args | |\n| Aider | `aider --message` | args | |\n| *Custom* | *any* | *configurable via YAML adapter* | |\n\nAdding a new agent requires **only a YAML configuration file** — no code changes.\n\n---\n\n## 🔌 claude-interactive Plugin\n\nThe `claude-interactive` plugin ships as a separate release asset. It wraps the Claude Code CLI in a PTY so workers run under your **Claude subscription** instead of consuming programmatic API credits.\n\n**How it works:** NEEDLE pipes subprocess stdio, which causes `claude` to detect a non-TTY and switch to API billing. `claude-interactive` creates an internal PTY so `claude` sees a real terminal, keeping it in interactive/subscription mode.\n\n**Install:**\n\n```bash\n# Download the latest claude-interactive release\ngh release download --repo jedarden/NEEDLE --pattern 'claude-interactive*'\nchmod +x claude-interactive-install.sh\n./claude-interactive-install.sh\n```\n\n**Requirements:** Python 3.10+, `pyte` (`pip install pyte`), and the `claude` CLI on PATH.\n\n**Run:**\n\n```bash\ncd /path/to/workspace\nneedle run --agent claude-interactive --count 4\n```\n\nSource lives in [`plugins/claude-interactive/`](plugins/claude-interactive/).\n\n---\n\n## 📁 Repository Structure\n\n```\nNEEDLE/\n├── Cargo.toml             # Trace capture, storage, retention\n│   ├── transcript/        # Session JSONL parsing, action-outcome extraction\n│   ├── types/             # Shared types, error definitions\n│   ├── upgrade/           # Self-update, hot-reload, rollback\n│   ├── validation/        # Pre-dispatch and post-execution checks\n│   └── worker/            # Worker session and identity management\n├── tests/                 # Integration tests\n├── ci/                    # Docker images used by GitHub Actions\n├── .github/workflows/     # CI + release pipelines\n├── config/                # Vendored gitleaks rules\n└── docs/                  # Plan, research, examples, post-mortems\n```\n\n---\n\n## 🔍 Observability\n\nNEEDLE emits structured telemetry for every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome. A silent worker is a broken worker.\n\n### Exported Signals\n\n| Signal | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| **Traces** | Spans for `worker.session`, `bead.lifecycle`, `bead.claim`, `agent.dispatch`, `strand.evaluated`, `outcome.handled` |\n| **Metrics** | `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.cost.usd`, and more |\n| **Logs** | All events not represented as spans, with severity mapping (`ERROR` for failures, `WARN` for stale peers) |\n\n### OpenTelemetry (OTLP) Export\n\nNEEDLE can export telemetry to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.) via OTLP.\n\n**Minimal configuration (`.needle.yaml`):**\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  otlp_sink:\n    enabled: true\n    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC, or :4318 for HTTP\n    protocol: \"grpc\"\n```\n\n**Semantic conventions:** NEEDLE follows OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions for LLM telemetry, enabling out-of-the-box integration with GenAI dashboards (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n\nSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) for the complete semantic mapping table.\n\n---\n\n## 📊 Production Status\n\nNEEDLE currently powers my own headless multi-agent workflow — workers run continuously against shared bead queues, dispatching to Claude Code and other CLIs, with full OTLP telemetry wired through. APIs are stable enough that I rebuild on top of them daily.\n\nThis is alpha software in the sense that **I'm the primary user**, not in the sense that \"it doesn't work.\" Resource governance is delegated to [claude-governor](https://github.com/jedarden/claude-governor); session monitoring is handled by [ccdash](https://github.com/jedarden/ccdash).\n\nIf you want to run NEEDLE in your own workflow, open an issue and I'll help.\n\n---\n\n## 🔗 Related Projects\n\n- **[claude-governor](https://github.com/jedarden/claude-governor)** — caps API spend and enforces weekly Anthropic quotas across NEEDLE worker fleets\n- **[ccdash](https://github.com/jedarden/ccdash)** — TUI for monitoring Claude Code sessions, token usage, and worker activity\n- **[CLASP](https://github.com/jedarden/CLASP)** — drop-in proxy letting Claude Code target OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, or any LLM backend\n- **[agentists-quickstart](https://github.com/jedarden/agentists-quickstart)** — opinionated DevPod workspaces for running Claude Code + NEEDLE\n\n---\n\n## 📄 License\n\nMIT\n","numLines":364,"startLine":1,"totalLines":364}}}
